question: I received an MSP letter after moving to Kelowna. A U.S. website tells me to contact Medicaid instead. Which health coverage system is relevant?
generated_answer:
Since you've moved to Kelowna, which is in British Columbia, Canada, the relevant health coverage system for you is the Medical Services Plan (MSP) of British Columbia. 

MSP is the provincial health insurance program that covers medically necessary services, including doctor visits, hospital stays, and other health care services. The letter you received is likely related to your enrollment or registration with MSP.

You can disregard the information about Medicaid, as it is a U.S.-based program and not relevant to your situation in Canada. Instead, you should follow up with the instructions provided in the MSP letter or contact the MSP directly to confirm your coverage and ensure you're properly enrolled.

To get more information or to contact MSP, you can visit their website at [www2.gov.bc.ca/gov/content/health/health-drug-coverage/msp](http://www2.gov.bc.ca/gov/content/health/health-drug-coverage/msp) or call their toll-free number: 1-877-950-3668.
